research_profile.summary_bio: Shama Abidi (MPhil in Pharmacy Practice, Department of Pharmacy Practice, Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of Karachi, Karachi, Pakistan) is a Senior Pharmacist / Clinical Pharmacist at Department of Pharmacy Services, Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi, Pakistan. Sample Size: N = 110 angina patients (61 male, 49 female; June 2022 - June 2023)
Key Evidence Summary: Evaluated Beta Blockers (BB, 36.36%), Calcium Channel Blockers (CCB, 54.4%), and CCB+BB combination (9.8%) in tertiary care cardiology OPDs using Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) and Naranjo ADR scale. Title: Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study
Authors: Fizzah Ali, Tabassum Zehra, Nazir Ahmed Solangi, Karim Ullah Makki, Haris Aziz Siddiqui, Shama Abidi
Journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 35, No. 6, November 2022, pp. 1595-1601)
DOI: 10.36721/PJPS.2022.35.6.REG.1595-1601.1
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: App#0592-2020 LNH-ERC (Liaquat National Hospital Ethical Committee)
Sample Size: N = 134 non-adherent carbapenem prescriptions in Medical ICU/HDU (Dec 2020 - May 2021)
Key Evidence Summary: Prospective interventional study at Liaquat National Hospital evaluating physician acceptance and clinical outcomes of pharmacist-led Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) interventions for carbapenem therapy. ASP interventions were accepted in 117/134 (87.3%) patients, resulting in 7-day clinical improvement in 99 (84.6%) patients and a significant reduction in 30-day readmission due to re-infection (p = 0.036). Interventions included renal dose adjustment for creatinine clearance (62.7%, n=84) and antibiotic de-escalation (25.4%, n=34).
